findings.fix: You hold the line for everyone, even for those who need an exception. Since one exception feels unfair to the rest, you give the rule in place of a second chance. Weigh what a rule costs someone, and hold the line only where it helps.

findings.quote: "the opening you see … the hand at home that opens"
findings.issue: open×4 on the page; "opens" here has an obvious swap.
findings.fix: Wood runs through your wealth, your family and your social life. It is the opening you see before the sign is up, the hand at home that gives before anyone asks, and the trip your friends still weigh while you are already packed.

findings.quote: "and hand the person you keep your presence ahead of your feelings"
findings.issue: "the person you keep" does not read as "your partner"; the clause also drops its subject.
findings.fix: Loyalty is how you love, given rather than said. You rate being loyal above speaking up, and you give the person you are with your presence ahead of your feelings. Say it once in plain words, because unspoken loyalty leaves them guessing.

findings.quote: "Saving comes before spending for you, and you never decide it."
findings.issue: "you never decide it" reads as a refusal; the sense is that it happens without a decision.
findings.fix: Saving comes before spending for you, without your ever deciding it. Being covered means more than anything you would buy, so you save ahead of wanting. Spend a small part of what you save on yourself, because a cushion is also for sitting on.

findings.quote: "Giving comes before being asked, for you."
findings.issue: The trailing ", for you" is an afterthought; it belongs at the front.
findings.fix: For you, giving comes before being asked. You feel most yourself with something to hand over, so you give ahead of knowing whether anyone needs it. Once you wait for a need to show, you give each gift to someone who wanted it.

findings.quote: "Holding a true thing in feels worse to you, so you speak"
findings.issue: An unfinished comparison: worse than what?
findings.fix: You speak up where silence would be easier. Holding a true thing in feels worse to you than saying it, so you speak rather than wait for a welcome. If you let a few conversations go cold, you get to keep speaking up as yourself.

findings.quote: "As a friction, intake outruns use and you take in more than you decide, your odd way or the way home taught you. You keep what you know where nobody learns it."
findings.issue: The first thing on three pages does not parse: the tail names the two gods' routes as if they were things taken in, and "where nobody learns it" is unclear.
findings.fix: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Growing is what Wood makes of it. As a friction, you take in more than you use, by your own odd route or the way home taught you. You keep what you know where nobody learns from it.

findings.quote: "you would rather puzzle an answer out alone than take one from a teacher. Either way you run dry"
findings.issue: "Either way" follows one way only; the Sage's face (pouring out to others) is missing, so the definition fits half the cell.
findings.fix: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Wood makes it grow. As a catalyst, the intake falls behind the output, so you puzzle answers out alone or pour what you know into others. Either way you run dry before you feel taught.

findings.quote: "You keep learning past the point of use because being judged feels worse than being unready."
findings.issue: The diagnosis is the Alchemist's alone; on the Sage page it sits under "Helps too soon", "Holds too tight" and "Stays put" and names nobody there.
findings.fix: Seek Metal, the Action energy. Metal is the finished line: it decides, it ships, it dates the thing you keep studying. Let it spend what Wood piles up. You hold on to what you take in, an idea or a person, past its use. Decide one open question by a written date. Hand someone one unfinished page.

findings.quote: "As a catalyst, much of you stays unsaid. You hold back a kind word or a bold idea"
findings.issue: The definition contradicts the ledger under it: "Gives first", "Always making", "Speaks up", "Stands out" and "Goes off script" all show Expression pouring out. The reader is told in one breath that they hold back and that they never stop speaking.
findings.fix: Your Expression is the gate where inner work becomes outer fact. Wood makes it grow. As a catalyst, the gate opens in bursts, a gift before anyone asks or a truth before its moment. Between bursts you go quiet and show your family only half of you.

findings.quote: "you want the next opening as much as a steady love. You do best once you choose one and finish it."
findings.issue: Wanting both does not describe a lack; the close prescribes (the advice's job) and leans on capacity ("You do best").
findings.fix: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Wood makes it grow, so what you build adds up. As a catalyst, your hands sit empty, so you reach for every new opening or hold tight to one safe thing. You build less than your strength could carry.

findings.quote: "You start more than your body has strength to finish."
findings.issue: This repeats the definition's "You wear yourself out before your plans are finished" and "Chases the new"; the diagnosis should add the cause that the cure answers.
findings.fix: Seek Metal, your own Body energy. Metal is what stays when the wanting stops, the rest under the effort. Let it hold what Wood pours out. You treat rest as time stolen from building. Sleep a full night ahead of any new yes. Eat before you plan the next thing.

findings.quote: "You give out faster than you take in, and running on your own fuel feels like energy until it runs out."
findings.issue: This restates the definition ("the intake falls behind the output … you run dry") one section later.
findings.fix: Taking in feels to you like falling behind, so you skip it. Take a class in something nobody pays you for. Keep one evening a week with no plans. Ask someone older how they did it and listen past the first sentence. Nap before the next idea.

findings.quote: "You carry more push than any one thing asks for."
findings.issue: A third "more than one thing needs" line on the page, after "You hold more of yourself than one load needs" (and "more go in you than a finish uses" on P003).
findings.fix: Seek Metal, the Order energy. Metal is the line that holds, a rule you did not write and a date you cannot move. Let it shape what Wood keeps growing. You trust your own line more than anyone else's. Give one plan to someone above you and take their deadline as final. Finish the small thing first.

findings.quote: "You hold more of yourself than one load needs, and you carry all of it instead of owing anyone a piece. You are allowed to owe someone a piece of the load."
findings.issue: "hold more of yourself than one load needs" is abstract, and "owe … a piece" is said twice in two sentences.
findings.fix: Asking comes last, well after the point where it would have worked. Owing anyone feels like losing ground, so you carry the whole load instead of sharing it. You are allowed to owe someone a piece of the load.

findings.quote: "Owing nobody feels safer to you, so you do the whole thing yourself sooner than hand off a piece."
findings.issue: This repeats the friction pole's "Asks no one" (the same act, the same cause, the same "piece"), so the two poles do not differ in direction; it also closes on advice (W-001).
findings.fix: Doing it alone is where your strength shows. You trust your own hands before anyone's plan, so you finish what others are still waiting on. You keep that strength with company beside you too.

findings.quote: "Where a sprint would get you in" · "since borrowed tempo is never yours"
findings.issue: "get you in" is unclear, "tempo" is above B2, and the reason goes round in a circle.
findings.fix: When a sprint would get you there, you keep your own pace instead. Being late on your terms sits better with you than being rushed on someone else's. You lose the chances that needed a sprint, and you chose that trade.

findings.quote: "you hand them the easier you, and consistency is none the poorer"
findings.issue: "none the poorer" is a C1 idiom, and "the easier you" is vague; the cost to friends never lands.
findings.fix: Holding yourself to one standard means holding friends to it. Staying the same matters more to you than meeting anyone halfway, so an off day gets no slack. You give your friends the same you every day, and none of the softness they need.

findings.quote: "You pay for going first in landings taken alone, and asking one person along changes that."
findings.issue: "landings taken alone" is a figure the reader has to decode, and the tail is advice.
findings.fix: You go first, with the plan half done and the vote not in. Waiting your turn feels like losing, since the opening is worth more to you than certainty. You get every opening first, and you land alone more often than you need to.

findings.quote: "You risk their savings along with your own whenever you bet too big."
findings.issue: The close restates the chip and sentence 2, in the "along with your own" formula (pattern 6).
findings.fix: Your biggest bets land on other people too. Going big matters more to you than going safe, so the shared money rides at your size of risk. You set the size of a risk that the people who pooled with you have to carry.

findings.quote: "You never reach the decision in the middle of a circle, and it never closes alone."
findings.issue: It is unclear what "it" is (the circle? the decision?), and "never … never" blurs the cost.
findings.fix: Thinking a question through means walking all the way around it first. Being certain weighs more with you than being quick, so you take one more angle rather than decide. You circle a question for weeks that a single choice would have closed.

findings.quote: "you spend years on what a teacher would hand you in a day. You pay in years for what one shown shortcut would give back."
findings.issue: The close says sentence 2 again, in harder words ("one shown shortcut").
findings.fix: Being self-taught makes the knowing yours. The long way feels more honest than the short, so you spend years on what a teacher would hand you in a day. You own every answer you have, and each cost you more time than it needed.

findings.quote: "Holding back feels more like respect than a nudge, so their nudge never comes. You hold back the push that would have moved them, and it is yours to give."
findings.issue: Push and nudge are said three times, and the tail "it is yours to give" is unclear.
findings.fix: When someone close to you grows slowly, you give them time instead of a push. Pushing feels to you like a lack of respect, so the nudge never comes. You hold back the one push that would have moved them.

findings.quote: "You lose every chance that arrives as a change, and you lose it by refusing to bend."
findings.issue: The second clause restates the first and the chip.
findings.fix: Never bending keeps you honest and keeps you tired. Since a new plan feels like being pushed, you hold your shape instead of saving your strength. You turn down every chance that arrives dressed as a change.

findings.quote: "you spread yourself over them, tired at each one. Spread this thin, you never get a full rest and start each day already tired."
findings.issue: spread×4 and tired×2 in 43 words; the close restates sentence 2.
findings.fix: You are spread over more things than your body can keep up with. Letting one go feels like losing, so you keep them all and arrive at each one tired. You never get a full rest, and you start each day already behind.

findings.quote: "You spend their quiet months as well as your own."
findings.issue: The reader cannot tell what "their quiet months" are; the cost to others does not land.
findings.fix: Spending on the people near you comes before your own next month. Helping them out feels better than keeping, so you cover their short weeks instead of a shared cushion. You spend the savings that would have carried you both through a lean month.

findings.quote: "so you stay rather than learn what leaving costs"
findings.issue: The logic is turned around: the reader stays because they fear what leaving costs, not to avoid learning it.
findings.fix: Leaving comes hard to you, so you stay where the giving back stopped. With more Wood than strength for it, you put more in rather than face leaving. You keep paying in effort every month to a place that returns none of it.

findings.quote: "you take the quick start ahead of the rest you are owed … every quick start costs you the rest you never get"
findings.issue: "rest" can be read as remainder or as sleep, and the real cost of quick starts (the unfinished middle) is named only in the instruction.
findings.fix: Whenever something new opens, you start before asking what it needs. Starting feels like freedom, so the slow middle of each thing gets less of you than the first day did. You pay for every quick start with the finishes you never reach.

findings.quote: "you are generous … being generous … Let them be generous sometimes, since your giving takes their chance to be generous."
findings.issue: generous×4 in 44 words.
findings.fix: When the people close to you run short, you give before being asked. Being the giver keeps you freer than being owed, so you give rather than build anything shared. You keep the giving one-way, and the people you help never get to give back.

findings.quote: "saving first costs you the today you never have"
findings.issue: "the today you never have" does not read at B1.
findings.fix: Your safety lives in what you have saved. Since you put feeling covered ahead of feeling alive, you save by postponing the small pleasures. You put off today's small joys for a tomorrow that keeps moving.

findings.quote: "Stay beside a finished thing until praise comes, since the credit you never collect is the cost."
findings.issue: "is the cost" is bolted on, and the instruction carries the meaning.
findings.fix: Stopping feels like disappearing, and making keeps you here. The joy for you is in the making, so you start something new the day the last one is done. You leave each finished thing before anyone thanks you for it, and the credit goes uncollected.

findings.quote: "Add a gentle push when it counts, because your relaxed patience lets a child grow sure of itself."
findings.issue: The reason argues against its own instruction (patience is why you should push?); the passage assumes a child (child×2, "itself").
findings.fix: With people who look to you, you keep things relaxed. Since you would rather be enjoyed than obeyed, you let a younger friend or a student set their own pace. You give them ease, and sometimes they needed the push you held back.

findings.quote: "Finish one plan unchanged, because that keeps the chances only a plain version wins."
findings.issue: The close does not parse, and it is advice (W-001).
findings.fix: Off script is how you stay interested. Sticking to a plan switches your talent off, so you change it halfway rather than see it through. You lose the results that only come to a plan carried out as written.

findings.quote: "You would rather see a child happy now than stretched"
findings.issue: A claim the reading cannot know: an 18 to 35 reader mostly has no child, and the line excludes them.
findings.fix: You put comfort first for the people in your care too. You would rather see them happy now than stretched, so you pick pleasant hours over useful ones. You trade the effort they would grow on for an hour of ease.

findings.quote: "Read one page you wrote to a child or a friend."
findings.issue: The same child assumption, on three more pages.
findings.fix: You lose more by waiting until a thing is ready than by showing it rough. Give the thing you made to someone before you think it is finished. Tell one person about a plan you have kept quiet. Read one page you wrote to a friend. Send the text without rereading it.
